newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO SELL TELECOMS, SPIRITS, ENERGY FIRMS IN 97.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO SELL TELECOMS, SPIRITS, ENERGY FIRMS IN 97.

text.p: Poland is likely to start privatising telecommunications, distilleries, chemical and energy companies -- the most sensitive sectors of the economy -- in 1997, Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
Kaczmarek told reporters on Monday before a government meeting that part of the companies' stock would be earmarked for Poland's programme of reforming the inefficient social security system.
"Next year privatisation will encompass the sensitive sectors of the economy -- telecommunications, energy, pharmaceuticals and distilleries," Kaczmarek said.
The government was due to discuss privatisation guidelines for 1997 at Monday's meeting.
"Next year will also be crucial for the usage of state assets in the social security reform," Kaczmarek said.
Kaczmarek said the budget expected to earn more than six billion zlotys from privatisation next year, against 2.37 billion zlotys in 1996.
"The budget's expectations from privatisation next year are much higher than this year," Kaczmarek said.
